body: From the 2009 trough, both compounded on Chinese wealth creation, price increases above inflation and supply-limited products (Birkin waitlists; Louis Vuitton never discounts). Hermès: ~€90 (2009) [unverified] -> ~€2,750 (Feb 2025) ≈ 30x; operating margin ~40%. LVMH: ~€40 (Mar 2009) [unverified] -> ~€900 (Apr 2023) ≈ 22x; Bernard Arnault briefly became world's richest. Split: mostly EPS (sales and margins up), plus P/E expansion to ~50x for Hermès and ~25-30x for LVMH [approx]. Side story: LVMH secretly built a ~17-23% Hermès stake via equity swaps (2010), fined by the AMF and distributed in 2014 — Hermès family formed a holding to lock control [from memory, unverified]. Reversal: May 2023 one-day $30bn luxury sell-off on US/China demand fears; China reopening bet faded; 2024 was a bad year for LVMH/Kering (Hermès held up); by Sept 2026 LVMH ~-55% from its 2023 peak (~-37% in 2026), out of Europe's top 10; Hermès down to ~€1,382 from ~€2,750 (date of quote unverified). EARLY SIGNAL visible ~2009-12: double-digit organic growth in Asia, price increases without volume loss, waitlists — pricing power. Who caught it: family owners (Arnault, Dumas/Puech); no documented outside name. LESSON: premiumisation compounders still carry demand cycles; Hermès (scarcity) held far better than LVMH (breadth) when the China aspirational buyer retreated, and a 50x P/E leaves no cushion.

data.early_signals: price hikes w/o volume loss, waitlists, Asian organic growth
data.lesson: scarcity beats breadth in luxury downturns; luxury is still cyclical

title: Hermès and LVMH 2009-2025: luxury pricing power, then the China reversal
